description: Golden repository-identity corpus (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 6). The connector reduces a checkout's remote to the canonical form and the control plane reduces what an operator typed; both must produce the same value, so both languages run this file. expect_canonical is what canonicaliseCloneUrl returns, expect_reason the stable failure it reports instead, and expect_sanitised what sanitiseCloneUrl leaves behind.

cases.name: https-clone-url
cases.note: The form a forge's copy button produces.

cases.name: ssh-scp-like
cases.note: Git's scp-like remote. The account name is not a credential, so sanitisation keeps it.

cases.name: ssh-url
cases.note: The same repository spelled as a URL. It must reduce to the same identity as the scp-like form.

cases.name: bare-host-and-path
cases.note: What a human types. No scheme, no colon, no suffix.

cases.name: default-https-port-dropped
cases.note: A port the scheme already implies is noise; keeping it would make one repository into two.

cases.name: default-ssh-port-dropped
cases.note: The same rule over SSH.

cases.name: non-default-port-kept
cases.note: A self-hosted forge on a non-default port is a different endpoint and the port is part of the identity.

cases.name: bare-host-with-port-is-not-scp-like
cases.note: host:8443/path is a host and a port, not Git's host:path. Reading it as scp-like would make 8443/platform/api the path.

cases.name: git-suffix-is-case-insensitive
cases.note: repo and repo.GIT are one repository on every forge.

cases.name: trailing-slash-dropped
cases.note: A trailing slash is a spelling difference, not a different repository.

cases.name: trailing-slash-after-git-suffix
cases.note: Both are removed, in that order.

cases.name: host-case-is-normalised
cases.note: A host name is case-insensitive.

cases.name: path-case-is-preserved
cases.note: Most forges treat the path as case-sensitive, so Example/Repo and example/repo may be two repositories.

cases.name: deep-group-hierarchy
cases.note: Self-hosted GitLab nests groups; every segment is part of the identity.

cases.name: https-token-is-dropped
cases.note: How every forge documents cloning with a personal access token. A bare userinfo outside SSH is a secret, not an account name (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

cases.name: uppercase-scheme-token-is-dropped
cases.note: The scheme comparison is case-insensitive, and sanitisation lowercases the scheme it rewrote.

cases.name: git-daemon-userinfo-is-dropped
cases.note: The git daemon protocol is unauthenticated and has no credential mechanism, so a userinfo there cannot be an account to log in as.

cases.name: ssh-username-is-kept
cases.note: The secret in an SSH remote is a key on disk. Dropping the account name would store a URL that does not clone.

cases.name: ssh-password-is-dropped
cases.note: A password in an SSH URL is still a credential.

cases.name: scp-like-password-is-dropped
cases.note: Sanitisation drops the pair. Canonicalisation splits at the first colon, so what is left is not a repository and is refused rather than guessed at.

cases.name: unsupported-scheme-still-loses-its-userinfo
cases.note: A scheme nothing accepts yet is treated as secret-bearing, because the predicate asks whether the URL is SSH rather than listing what leaks.

cases.name: file-scheme-is-refused
cases.note: A path on one machine is not an identity another machine can resolve.

cases.name: empty
cases.note: Nothing to normalise.

cases.name: whitespace-only
cases.note: Trimmed to nothing.

cases.name: leading-and-trailing-whitespace-is-trimmed
cases.note: A pasted value keeps its surrounding whitespace; the repository is the same one.

cases.name: interior-whitespace-is-refused
cases.note: A space inside a remote is a paste accident, not a repository.

cases.name: control-character-is-refused
cases.note: Control characters never belong in a remote.

cases.name: delete-character-is-refused
cases.note: U+007F is refused with the C0 range it sits beside.

cases.name: over-length
cases.note: Longer than the schema's 512-character clone-URL bound, so it is refused before anything is parsed.

cases.name: canonical-over-length
cases.note: Short enough to parse and too long to store: the canonical form exceeds the schema's 255-character bound.

cases.name: host-without-a-path
cases.note: A host alone names no repository.

cases.name: bare-host-without-a-path
cases.note: The same without a scheme.

cases.name: scp-like-without-a-path
cases.note: The colon is there and the path is not.

cases.name: path-that-is-only-a-git-suffix
cases.note: Removing the suffix leaves an empty segment, which is not a repository name.

cases.name: empty-host
cases.note: Dropping the userinfo leaves no host at all.

cases.name: uppercase-path-segment-with-permitted-punctuation
cases.note: The canonical character class permits letters, digits, dot, underscore, tilde and hyphen in a path segment.
